memory_candidates.content: When auditing a docs tree for broken relative links, a throwaway resolver (walk every *.md, extract ](path) targets excluding http(s)/mailto/anchor-only, resolve against the containing file's own directory, flag non-existent targets) reliably surfaces systemic bugs like a README.md vs docs-README.md naming mismatch producing a dozen+ identical breadcrumb defects. Always document a merge-time-generated-file exclusion class (e.g. CLAUDE.md) separately from a file_scope-excluded SOURCE file's own broken links -- these are two distinct exclusion classes with different justifications and must not be conflated in the acceptance criterion.

When a structural docs-correctness task must avoid touching several other open records' substantive territory, a Boundary Register (per-site deferral list with each site's owning record cited, plus a small set of individually-reviewed 'close call' micro-edits that touch only an invocation surface or illustrative sample data, never the underlying assertion) keeps the two concerns cleanly separated. A close call should carry a pre-edit grep/check with a conditional-abort path (e.g. grep scripts for a message string before rewording doc prose that describes it) rather than assuming the doc and the code already agree.

verify-deploy.sh's TARGET argument must be a directory containing a deployed .claude/ tree (TARGET/.claude), not an extension's own source_dir -- passing the source_dir directly (e.g. agent-system/extensions/core) errors 'no deploy tree' before any gate runs. For a source-store-only check like --only-gate 3,4 (doc-lint, task-reference-lint), pass the repo root instead, since the repo root both has the deployed .claude/ and is itself the source-store repo those gates inspect.
